title: Sunday Soup
summary: Weeks nine and ten. Théo wants something that doesn't exist, so he makes it. He finally tells his sister the truth. And for the first time, Théo himself starts to glow. Ends with 11 lights.

screens.image: Théo's kitchen, grey-cream now, the Who Is Théo? map pinned on the fridge with the player's items drawn on it.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Week nine. Théo looks at his map. The biggest landmark on it, by far, is a pan.

screens.image: Close on the pan landmark. Small figures drawn around it, eating.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: It's not cooking he misses, exactly. It's cooking for people. A full table. Somebody saying "ah, c'est bon, ça" with their mouth full.

screens.image: Théo on his phone, searching; the screen cold blue. Search results drawn as cards: "Cuisine solidaire du quartier: FERMÉ".

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: He looks for somewhere to cook for people. A community kitchen: closed last year. A supper club: forty euros a seat, fully booked until spring.

screens.image: The Critic, lounging on the phone screen.

words.speaker: Critic
words.text: See? It doesn't exist. Nothing ever exists for people like you.

screens.image: Four cream cards on a black page: a magnifying glass, a signpost, a speech bubble, a seed.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: When the thing you need doesn't exist, there are four doors.

objects.label: Magnifying glass
objects.line: Search wider: the next town, an online group, something similar.

objects.label: Signpost
objects.line: Join something next door to it: a library event, a community hall, a class.

objects.label: Speech bubble
objects.line: Ask one person: "Do you know where people go to...?"

screens.image: Théo knocking at Madame Roux's door, warm light.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Théo tries door three first. He asks Madame Roux.

screens.image: Madame Roux in her doorway, finger raised.

words.speaker: Madame Roux
words.text: In my day, people just cooked a big pot and knocked on doors. The courtyard is empty on Sundays. Nobody will stop you. I will bring the chairs.

screens.image: Théo at his table writing a note in big hand lettering.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: So it's door four.

interaction.prefill: SOUPE DU DIMANCHE. Courtyard, Sunday 1pm. Free. Bring a bowl. — Théo, 3rd floor

screens.image: The note taped to the building's front door, among other notices.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: He tapes it to the front door. Then takes it down. Then tapes it back up.

screens.image: Saturday night: Théo cooking a huge pot. Steam drawn warm. Onions, carrots, a bouquet garni.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Saturday night he cooks enough soup for twenty people. Just in case. Also because he panicked.

objects.label: Leeks
objects.line: Leeks, washed twice, because grit is unforgivable.

objects.label: Carrots
objects.line: Carrots, for colour. The first colour in the pot.

objects.label: Herbs
objects.line: A bouquet garni: thyme, bay, parsley stalks, tied with string.

screens.image: Sunday 1pm. The courtyard: grey stone, a pot on a camping stove, five folding chairs, Théo alone.
screens.caption: 1:00 pm

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Sunday, 1pm. Nobody.

screens.image: 1:10pm. Still alone. The Critic sitting on one of the chairs.
screens.caption: 1:10 pm

words.speaker: Critic
words.text: Told you.

screens.image: Théo ladling himself a bowl, sitting down.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Marie-Clo said: if nobody comes, you still do the thing. Théo eats a bowl of soup in a courtyard. It's good soup.

screens.image: 1:20pm. Madame Roux arriving with a folding chair and a cake tin. Madame Roux's light grows brighter.
screens.caption: 1:20 pm

words.speaker: Madame Roux
words.text: Sorry, I was doing my hair. For a party you have to do your hair.

screens.image: A shy man in his 40s in the archway, holding a baguette, half-hidden.
screens.caption: 1:25 pm

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: 1:25pm. A man Théo has passed on the stairs a hundred times and never spoken to.

screens.image: Yann offering the bread awkwardly.

words.speaker: Yann
words.text: I saw the note. I didn't know if... I brought bread. Is that... is bread okay?

options.label: "Sit, sit, I made enough for twenty."

screens.image: Yann sitting, eating, eyes closing at the taste.

words.speaker: Yann
words.text: I live alone since my divorce. I haven't eaten soup someone else made in... two years? Maybe.

interaction.text: Yann, 2nd floor: lives alone since his divorce. Brings bread.

screens.image: Trois-Pattes bursting into the courtyard, Sophie behind in her yellow raincoat.

words.speaker: Sophie
words.text: He smelled it from the street. I'm so sorry. Is there enough for a very rude dog?

screens.image: Four people and a dog around the pot. And Théo, ladling, his outline glowing for the first time. Théo's own outline gains a permanent soft glow.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: And then something happens that hasn't happened in this story before. Théo starts to glow.

screens.image: Close on Théo serving Yann a second bowl, warm light on both faces.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Not because someone gave him something. Because he gave something. Some people light up when they're loved. Théo lights up when he's loving.

screens.image: Evening. Théo washing a mountain of bowls, smiling.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Four people. Twenty portions of soup. Théo is going to be eating soup until Thursday. He doesn't mind.

screens.image: Théo on his sofa, phone in hand, Camille's name on the screen.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: That night, he calls Camille. Not a text. A call.

screens.image: Split panel: Théo on his sofa; Camille in her kitchen, phone at her ear, big scarf.

words.speaker: Camille
words.text: Hey! You called! Are you okay?

screens.image: Same split panel, Camille's face knowing.

words.speaker: Camille
words.text: Théo. It's me.

screens.image: The split panel, the line between them breaking: warm light flowing across. Camille's light grows.

words.speaker: Théo
words.text: Honestly? It's been really bad. I couldn't eat for two days. And the {chased}... it's over. I didn't tell anyone.

screens.image: Camille, eyes wet, smiling.

words.speaker: Camille
words.text: Thank you for telling me. I've been so worried. Can I come visit? I'll bring wine. You bring soup. Obviously.

screens.image: Théo after the call, lying on the sofa, lighter.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: It turns out saying the true thing out loud makes it a little smaller. And it makes the people who love you a little closer.

screens.image: Light Map: a whole courtyard of lights, and Théo's own window glowing.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Eleven lights. One of them is Théo's.

screens.image: Quest card.

interaction.title: Tell one person the truth
interaction.text: Message or call someone who cares about you and tell them honestly how it's been. One sentence is enough: "Honestly, it's been rough."

interaction.title: Cook for someone
interaction.text: Cook for someone, or bring them something.
